public_rationale: This is a conditional forecast. It says that once AI usage drops, the revenue that has flowed into big tech will fall and acres of data centers will sit unused. Under the contract, the claim is scored only after a documented broad drop in AI usage. The cited evidence does not document such a drop. TechCrunch reported on 2025-10-06 that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said ChatGPT had 800 million weekly active users (e1). The same report said OpenAI had 500 million weekly users at the end of March 2025 and said in August 2025 that it was close to 700 million (e2). These figures show no drop between March and October 2025. The packet has no usage data after October 2025, so a later drop is not ruled out. Microsoft reported revenue of $76.4 billion for the quarter ended June 30, 2025, up 18% year over year (e3). This covers one company for one quarter. It is context only and does not test the second half of the claim. Because the evidence does not establish the antecedent, the claim cannot be scored.
limitations: The usage evidence covers only ChatGPT. It is OpenAI's own figures as reported by TechCrunch, not broad industry usage data.
The usage figures are three points in time (end of March, August and October 2025). They do not show usage between those points or after October 2025.
The packet cannot show whether AI usage fell between October 2025 and the evaluation date of 2026-10-28.
The revenue evidence covers Microsoft only, for the quarter ended June 30, 2025. It does not show big-tech revenue as a whole or in later periods.
The packet has no evidence on data-center utilization or idle capacity.

statement.excerpt: Once usage drops, so will the remarkable amounts of revenue that have flowed into big tech, and so will acres of data centers sit unused, the cloud equivalent of the massive overhiring we saw in post-lockdown Silicon Valley.

from_speaker: so will the remarkable amounts of revenue that have flowed into big tech
acres of data centers sit unused
our_interpretation: This is a conditional forecast. The antecedent is a clear, broad drop in AI usage, for example falling user counts or API volumes at major AI services.

The consequent: big tech's total revenue (not just AI revenue, since the speaker did not narrow it) falls, and large completed data-center capacity sits idle. Cancelled or delayed construction is not the same as built capacity sitting unused.
The claim can be scored only if the usage drop has happened.
criteria.support_condition: After a documented broad drop in AI usage, big-tech revenue falls and large completed data-center capacity goes unused.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After a documented broad drop in AI usage, big-tech revenue does not fall, or data centers stay well used.
